plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of a dark central disc surrounded by bright yellow ray petals. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is widely cultivated for seeds, oil, and ornamental use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America, Europe, and Central Asia; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west in a movement called heliotropism, but mature blooms generally stay facing east.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower forming dense clumps of tall stems topped with plumes of tiny golden flowers. It thrives in meadows, roadsides, and prairies, and provides vital late-season nectar and pollen for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time and releases airborne pollen.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like pink-lilac flowers in late summer and early fall without any leaves present. The strap-shaped leaves appear the following spring, after which they die back.
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe; cultivated in gardens in temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The plant contains colchicine, a toxic compound used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden-yellow flower balls. It blooms as the Southern Hemisphere winter transitions into spring, brightening the bush with bold color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to September)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
